newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end up on cue from Dow.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end up on cue from Dow.

text.p: Lifted by buying in most blue chips and selected secondliners, the Philippine equities market finished up on Tuesday by 38.22 points, or 1.24 percent at 3,128.38 points.
"Its the recovery in the U.S. that carried the momentum in the local market. We will see the resistance building up to 3,150," said Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities.
"Its a return to the bullishness. We were just affected by the Dow which wiped out earlier losses Monday night," said Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Securities Inc.

Traders said the decision of the Philippine Supreme Court allowing an anti-graft court to rule on the petition of businessman Eduardo Cojuangco to oust eight government nominees at the San Miguel board had no impact on San Miguel shares.
San Miguel A shares closed steady at 52 pesos a share. The two peso rise in San Miguel B shares to 110 pesos was attributed to the general uptrend of the market.
Total volume of shares traded amounted to 7.466 billion with value at 2.341 billion pesos. All sectors rose except the banking and financial sector.
Gainers outnumbered decliners 80 to 41 with 63 counters were unchanged.
"We might see a strong opening tommorrow and then some pullback late in the session," predicted Liu.
